  "relation": "REFINED",
  "consensus_summary": "Primary meaning of faith is personal trusting reliance on God/Christ (esp. for justification/salvation), not bare assent; common alternatives include faithfulness/allegiance (pistis Christou, emunah), the objective body of doctrine, a Spirit gift, or living faith shown in works.",
  "book_summary": "Faithfulness defined as obedience held steady by hope in the promise, illustrated by “faith without works is dead”; the common trust/justification sense is noted separately.",
  "rationale": "The book’s definition is compatible with the widely attested alternative of faith-as-faithfulness plus James’s living-faith emphasis, yet it materially narrows and sharpens the primary consensus (trust/reliance) into a specific obedience-sustained-by-hope formulation while relegating the justification-by-faith sense to a side note.",
  "citation_support": "PARTIAL",
  "strongest_objection": "The entry displaces the settled primary sense of saving trust with an obedience-centered reading that risks equating faith with works, even though Hab 2:4 and Jas 2:17 are also used by the consensus to support trust and living faith.",
  "confidence": "medium"
}
